name: Pi
short: A small, hackable coding agent for your terminal that works with many AI models. Version 1.0 shipped on 1 October.
what: A minimal coding agent for your terminal, like Claude Code or Codex CLI, that works with many AI model providers. You can extend it with skills, extensions, prompt templates and themes. Version 1.0 came out on 1 October 2026.
who: Developers who want one coding agent they can point at any model and customise. It deliberately leaves out sub-agents and plan mode, so it has fewer guardrails than the big-name agents.
needs: Node.js 22.19 or later. The Mac, Linux and Windows installers can install it for you
A subscription or API key from an AI provider. You connect it inside Pi with /login

steps.title: Start it in a project and log in
steps.text: Then type `/login` to connect your provider. Update later with `pi update`.

try.label: Suggested
try.text: Explain what this project does and list its main files.

watch: Pi has no permission system. It runs with your user's full access to files, programs and the network. For isolation, the README points to running it in a container.
The README invites you to publish your open-source sessions to Hugging Face. That's optional, and sessions can contain code and secrets.
The installer pipes a script into your shell. Read it first if you're unsure.
